label: Progress bar value pair
summary: A game function of the GUI that returns a whole number and takes two arguments; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name, it has to do with the values of a progress bar. The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: Qualification threshold
summary: The qualification threshold for PTV (progress to victory), read from the activity the GUI is about.
details: It is a shortcut for reading the activity's saved variable `progress_to_victory_threshold`. The game's own description only calls it the qualification PTV threshold.

label: Puppet action type
summary: Looks up a puppet action type by its key in the game's database.
details: You give it the key as text. The game lists its return type only as a null placeholder, so what the result offers is not documented; nothing in the game's texts uses it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the puppet action type.

label: Puppet type
summary: Looks up a puppet type by its key in the game's database.
details: Vanilla texts do not call it with a key. They use the form on a puppet entry or a puppet interaction group (`PuppetEntry.GetPuppetType`) and print the result's name, in the scheme window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the puppet type.

label: Red part of a 4-value vector
summary: The R part of a vector of four decimal numbers; going by the name, the red part of a color.
details: Going by its name, the R is the red component of a color-like four-part value. It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Red of 4 whole numbers
summary: The R part of a vector of four whole numbers; going by the name, the red part of a color.
details: Going by its name, the R is the red component. It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Raid intent
summary: Gives a raid intent; vanilla uses it on the army window.
details: The game documents it as a lookup of a raid intent by key. Vanilla uses it only without an argument, as `ArmyWindow.GetRaidIntent`, to set the data of a part of the army window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the raid intent, as the game documents it.

label: Random menu illustration
summary: Gives a picture for the front-end (start menu) screens; going by its name, a randomly chosen one.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of the multiplayer game setup and the multiplayer menu screens.

label: Random log info
summary: A text of log information, shown after the multiplayer checksum in the game's version info.
details: Vanilla shows it in the version line of the top bar and in the tooltip about game modules. What exactly the text holds is not documented; the 'random' and 'log' come from the name.

label: Relation
summary: Looks up a relation type (like friend or best friend) by its key.
details: Vanilla texts call `GetReasonFor` on the result and give it two characters, in the descriptions of messages about a friend, best friend or rival relation being set.

label: Religion
summary: Gives a religion; the game documents only that it takes one argument.
details: Vanilla texts do not call it with a key. They use the form on a faith (`GetFaith.GetReligion`) and print the religion's name or its family.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not named by the game; going by the other lookups, probably a key.

label: Religion by key
summary: Gives the religion with the given key.
details: Vanilla texts use it to print a religion's adjective, for example in the names of relics: 'Christian Relic'. Give it the religion key with its suffix, like 'christianity_religion'.

label: Religion family
summary: Looks up a religion family (a group of related religions) by its key.
details: Vanilla texts use it to print a family's name, for example 'rf_abrahamic'.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the religion family.

label: Religion type
summary: Looks up a religion type by its key in the game's database.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the religion type.

label: Screen resolution
summary: Gives the screen size, adjusted for the aspect ratio, as a two-part value.
details: Going by its name and its single use, it gives a width and height. Vanilla uses it as the size of an element in the bookmarks screen of the start menu.

label: Rite by key
summary: Gives the rite with the given key.
details: Vanilla texts use it to print a rite's name, for example in decisions that convert to a rite and in a text about adopting one as a personal rite.

label: Rite type
summary: Looks up a rite type by its key in the game's database.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the rite type.

label: Hovered court artifact
summary: The artifact the mouse is over in the royal court view.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it as the data of a part of the royal court window and of the court scene editor.

label: Hovered court character
summary: The character the mouse is over in the royal court view.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it as the data of a part of the royal court window and of the court scene editor.

label: Selected court artifact
summary: The artifact currently selected in the court scene editor.
details: Going by its name and its single use in the court scene editor window.

label: Selected court character
summary: The character currently selected in the court scene editor.
details: Going by its name and its single use in the court scene editor window.

label: Scene settings name
summary: The name of a court scene settings entry, as text.
details: Vanilla passes it the court scene settings of the court scene editor and shows the result as text and tooltip.

label: Scheme type
summary: Gives the scheme type with the given key.
details: Vanilla texts use it to print a scheme's name, for example 'murder' in the AI personality explanations.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the scheme type.

label: Scheme countermeasure type
summary: Looks up a scheme countermeasure type by its key in the game's database.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the countermeasure type.

label: Scheme odds frame
summary: Turns a scheme success value into the number of the frame that shows its odds level.
details: Vanilla feeds it the predicted odds of an interaction scheme and uses the whole number as the frame of a GUI element.

label: Scheme odds level name
summary: Turns a scheme success value into the name of its odds level, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the text that shows the predicted difficulty of a scheme interaction.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a number from the scheme prediction

label: Scheme pulse action
summary: Looks up a scheme pulse action by its key in the game's database.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the pulse action.

label: Scheme type
summary: Looks up a scheme type by its key in the game's database.
details: Vanilla texts mostly call it on a scheme (`scheme.GetSchemeType`) to ask things like whether it is a contract, which picks between two texts.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the scheme type.

label: Script value breakdown
summary: Shows a breakdown of how a named script value comes out for a character.
details: It is a shortcut: the target is turned into a scope and that scope's description of the script value is printed. Vanilla uses it in the cardinals window with the papal priority values of a character.

fields.name: Target
fields.text: The character the value is worked out for; it becomes the root.

fields.name: ScriptValueName
fields.text: The name of the script value.

label: Scripted character by history ID
summary: Gives the character with the given history ID, a character defined in the game's history files.
details: Vanilla texts use it to print the name of such a character in decisions and game rules.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The history ID of the character.

label: Scripted GUI
summary: Gives the scripted GUI (a GUI behavior defined in script) with the given name.
details: Vanilla GUI files use it as the data of a window part, or call things like `IsShown` on it to decide whether something is visible for a character.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the scripted GUI.

label: Scripted relation
summary: Looks up a scripted relation by its key in the game's database.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the scripted relation.

label: Scripted relation tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of a scripted relation between an owner and a target character.
details: It joins two parts with a blank line: the relation's description, then the reason it holds between the two. Vanilla uses it in the character window and on portraits.

fields.name: Owner
fields.text: The owner of the relation, the first character of the pair.

fields.name: Target
fields.text: The other character of the pair.

label: Secret type
summary: Looks up a secret type by its key.
details: Vanilla texts use it to print the secret's name, for example in crime confession texts about murder.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the secret type.

label: Segmented chance bar
summary: Builds the data for a progress bar split into segments that also shows a chance.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it as the data of bars in the HUD and the inspirations window, with defines for the maximum progress and the number of frames, and a scheme example in a shared GUI file. It takes four arguments; the game does not name them.

label: Segmented target bar
summary: Builds the data for a progress bar split into segments that marks a target.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it as the data of bars in the holy site windows and the Christian church window. In the lines shown the first argument is a maximum or threshold. It takes three arguments; the game does not name them.

label: Server info
summary: The information about the multiplayer server of the current session.
details: Vanilla uses it on the lobby view to get the server's name and whether it is an invite.

label: Situation
summary: Looks up a situation by its key, for example 'dynastic_cycle'.
details: Vanilla texts use the result to ask for its participant groups.

label: Situation catalyst type
summary: Looks up a situation catalyst type by its key in the game's database.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the catalyst type.

label: Situation group type
summary: Looks up a situation group type by its key in the game's database.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the group type.

label: Situation of type
summary: Gives the situation of a given situation type.
details: Vanilla uses it in the dynastic cycle and natural disaster windows, passing the type of the window's situation.

label: Situation type
summary: Looks up a situation type by its key in the game's database.
details: Vanilla texts use the result to reach the situation's phases, for example the phases of the dynastic cycle.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the situation type.

label: Smart brush interpolation names
summary: Gives the names of the interpolation modes of the map editor's smart material painter.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it. The game describes it as part of the map editor's smart material painter.

label: Smart brush pattern names
summary: Gives the names of the patterns of the map editor's smart material painter.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it. The game describes it as part of the map editor's smart material painter.

label: Spiritual fulfillment type
summary: Looks up a spiritual fulfillment type by its key in the game's database.
details: Vanilla uses the character form (`Character.GetSpiritualFulfillmentType`) as the data of a HUD part, not this key lookup.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the fulfillment type.

label: Static modifier
summary: Looks up a static modifier by its key in the game's database.
details: Vanilla GUI files use the form on a modifier item or scheme modifier to get its static modifier and print its name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the static modifier.

label: String setting text
summary: The text of a string setting from the game's settings.
details: Vanilla uses it in the settings window, passing the setting being shown.

label: Rectangle (decimal) as text
summary: Turns a rectangle of decimal numbers into text.
details: Going by its name and return type. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Rectangle (whole) as text
summary: Turns a rectangle of whole numbers into text.
details: Going by its name and return type. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Text as string
summary: Turns a piece of text into a plain string.
details: Vanilla uses it in the event window's animation tool, wrapping the selected text of a property search list before it is copied or shown.

label: 2-value vector as text
summary: Turns a vector of two decimal numbers into text.
details: Going by its name and return type. The game's texts do not use it.

label: 2-value int vector as text
summary: Turns a vector of two whole numbers into text.
details: Going by its name and return type. The game's texts do not use it.

label: 3-value vector as text
summary: Turns a vector of three decimal numbers into text.
details: Going by its name and return type. The game's texts do not use it.

label: 3-value int vector as text
summary: Turns a vector of three whole numbers into text.
details: Going by its name and return type. The game's texts do not use it.

label: 4-value vector as text
summary: Turns a vector of four decimal numbers into text.
details: Going by its name and return type. The game's texts do not use it.

label: 4-value int vector as text
summary: Turns a vector of four whole numbers into text.
details: Going by its name and return type. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Struggle
summary: Looks up a struggle by its key.
details: Vanilla texts use the result to print the struggle's name, for example 'persian_struggle' or 'iberian_struggle', in oath decisions.

label: Struggle phase
summary: Looks up a struggle phase by its key in the game's database.
details: Vanilla GUI files use the form on a catalyst history entry (`CatalystHistory.GetStrugglePhase`) to compare it with the struggle's current leading phase.

label: Struggle type
summary: Looks up a struggle type by its key in the game's database.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the struggle type.

label: Subject contract group
summary: Looks up a subject contract group by its key.
details: Vanilla texts use it to print the group's name in war results, with keys like 'tributary_mandala', as in 'X becomes your ...'.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the contract group.

label: Subject contract type
summary: Looks up a subject contract type by its key in the game's database.
details: Vanilla texts use it with a key such as 'special_contract' and then call `GetObligationName` on it to print the name of an obligation, in the vassal contract descriptions.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the contract type.

label: Suggestion type
summary: Looks up a suggestion type by its key in the game's database.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the suggestion type.

label: Character's progress to victory
summary: The target character's PTV (progress to victory) value.
details: It is a shortcut for reading that character's saved variable `progress_to_victory`.

label: Task contract type
summary: Looks up a task contract type by its key.
details: Vanilla texts call `GetName` on it to print a task contract's name, for example in hints about actions and in war messages.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the task contract type.

label: Tax slot obligation
summary: Looks up a tax slot obligation by its key in the game's database.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: Tax slot type
summary: Looks up a tax slot type by its key in the game's database.
details: Vanilla texts use the form on a tax slot (`TaxSlot.GetTaxSlotType`) to print things like the tax collector aptitude.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the tax slot type.

label: Tenet type
summary: Looks up a tenet (a faith's belief) by its key.
details: Vanilla texts use it to print a tenet's name, for example 'tenet_confession'. They call `GetName` on it and often give a rite as its argument.

label: Terrain
summary: Looks up a terrain type by its key.
details: Vanilla texts use the result to print the terrain's name, for example in building requirements and memory texts.

label: Ticks since last progress
summary: The number of game ticks since an activity last made progress, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as a value in the activity window, with the activity's ID and the number of days per week. It returns a whole number.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The activity; vanilla passes its ID.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Not named by the game; vanilla passes the days per week.

label: Time until anyone can unpause
summary: The seconds left before everyone, not only the one who paused, may unpause the game.
details: Vanilla uses it in the multiplayer pause message: 'Only I can unpause the game for N more seconds'.

label: Time between dates
summary: A text that tells how much time lies between two dates, in days or months.
details: Vanilla uses it in activity event texts and in the activity list window.

label: Time from days
summary: A text that tells a number of days into the future, in days or months.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts about waiting times, such as 'can only send a gift once every 5 years' and the wait before adopting another court language.

label: Title by key
summary: Gives the title with the given key.
details: Vanilla texts use it to print a title's name, for example 'd_cumbria' in a decision text.

label: Toggle companion AI command
summary: The game command that switches the AI control of companions on or off.
details: Going by its name and its use: vanilla passes it to `PostCommand` from a button in the military window.

label: Days in month
summary: The number of days in a given month.
details: Give 1 for January, 2 for February and so on. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Tournament prize category
summary: The option category of the tournament prizes.
details: It is a shortcut for the 'tournament_option_prizes' category of the tournament activity type.

label: Tournament prize level
summary: The prize level chosen for the tournament.
details: It is a shortcut for the option the activity has active in the prize category. Vanilla uses it to pick texts about the likely rewards of a contest and as a frame number in tournament GUI widgets.

label: Trait
summary: Looks up a trait by its key.
details: Vanilla texts use it very often to print a trait's name, for example in achievement descriptions.

label: Trait by index
summary: Gives the trait at a given position in the list of traits.
details: Going by its name and its single use in the multiplayer lobby, which passes a whole number.

label: Trait group
summary: Looks up a trait group by its key.
details: Vanilla uses it in the ledger to find which trait a character has from a group, for example 'education_stewardship'.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the trait group.

label: Traits
summary: The list of traits of the thing it is used on.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list shown for an accolade or for a character in guest and tax collector lists.

label: Traits with flag
summary: The list of traits that carry a given flag.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: Traits without flag
summary: The list of traits that do not carry a given flag.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: Travel option
summary: Looks up a travel option by its key.
details: Vanilla texts use it to print the option's name in building descriptions, for example 'fancy_mounts_option'.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the travel option.

label: Travel point of interest type
summary: Looks up a travel point of interest type by its key in the game's database.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: Triggered legend seed
summary: Looks up a triggered legend seed by its key in the game's database.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the legend seed.

label: Tutorial
summary: Gives access to the game's tutorial.
details: It is a promote: it turns the global context into the tutorial object. The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: Variable time remaining
summary: The time left until a saved timed variable runs out.
details: Going by its name and vanilla's use: texts use it with a date in cooldown messages, such as 'this task cannot be initiated until ...'. It returns a whole number.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The scope that holds the variable.

label: Variable system
summary: Gives the global variable system of the GUI.
details: Vanilla GUI files use it as the data of windows, for example the interaction confirmation window. The game documents nothing more.

label: Vassal stance
summary: Looks up a vassal stance by its key.
details: Vanilla texts use the key form with 'glory_hound' and the form on a character (`Character.GetVassalStance`) to print the stance's icon and name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the vassal stance.

label: View history tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the 'view history' button.
details: Going by its name; vanilla uses it as the tooltip in the character and confederation windows.

label: Fourth part of a 4-value vector
summary: The fourth (w) number of a vector of four decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Fourth of 4 whole numbers
summary: The fourth (w) number of a vector of four whole numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Wit contest aptitude
summary: How good the character is at the wit contest, as a script value.
details: It is a shortcut for the contest aptitude 'contest_type_aptitude_wit' of the character the GUI is about. Vanilla uses it in the tournament widgets.

label: First part of a 2-value vector
summary: The first (x) number of a vector of two decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: First of 2 whole numbers
summary: The first (x) number of a vector of two whole numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: First part of a 3-value vector
summary: The first (x) number of a vector of three decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: First of 3 whole numbers
summary: The first (x) number of a vector of three whole numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: First part of a 4-value vector
summary: The first (x) number of a vector of four decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: First of 4 whole numbers
summary: The first (x) number of a vector of four whole numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Second part of a 2-value vector
summary: The second (y) number of a vector of two decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Second of 2 whole numbers
summary: The second (y) number of a vector of two whole numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Second part of a 3-value vector
summary: The second (y) number of a vector of three decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Second of 3 whole numbers
summary: The second (y) number of a vector of three whole numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Second part of a 4-value vector
summary: The second (y) number of a vector of four decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Second of 4 whole numbers
summary: The second (y) number of a vector of four whole numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Third part of a 3-value vector
summary: The third (z) number of a vector of three decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Third of 3 whole numbers
summary: The third (z) number of a vector of three whole numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Third part of a 4-value vector
summary: The third (z) number of a vector of four decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Third of 4 whole numbers
summary: The third (z) number of a vector of four whole numbers.
details: Going by its name. It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Zoom level
summary: A game function that returns a whole number, most likely the current zoom level.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: Part of a 2-value vector
summary: Reads one number, by position, from a vector of two decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name and its two arguments (the vector and the position). It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Part of a 2-value int vector
summary: Reads one number, by position, from a vector of two whole numbers.
details: Going by its name and its two arguments (the vector and the position). It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Part of a 3-value vector
summary: Reads one number, by position, from a vector of three decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name and its two arguments (the vector and the position). It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Part of a 3-value int vector
summary: Reads one number, by position, from a vector of three whole numbers.
details: Going by its name and its two arguments (the vector and the position). It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Part of a 4-value vector
summary: Reads one number, by position, from a vector of four decimal numbers.
details: Going by its name and its two arguments (the vector and the position). It returns a decimal number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Part of a 4-value int vector
summary: Reads one number, by position, from a vector of four whole numbers.
details: Going by its name and its two arguments (the vector and the position). It returns a whole number. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Graphics skins
summary: Gives all the available graphics skins.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: Set graphics skin
summary: Makes the given graphics skin the active one.
details: It returns nothing. The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: Is graphics skin active
summary: Whether the given graphics skin is the active one.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: Glossary
summary: A text function with two arguments, used all over the game's concept descriptions.
details: Vanilla uses it very often in the texts of game concepts, for example in the barter goods and casus belli descriptions. What it prints is not documented; it is probably a glossary entry for the given key.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not named by the game; vanilla passes a word, like 'rattan'.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: Not named by the game; vanilla passes an uppercase key, like 'RATTAN_GLOSS'.

label: Go to start menu
summary: Goes back to the game's start menu from the multiplayer interface.
details: It returns nothing. The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: At least (decimal)
summary: Whether the first fixed-point number is greater than or equal to the second.
details: Vanilla uses it inside texts, often as the check of a text choice, for example for progress to victory in the tournament and for hegemon stability.

label: At least (float)
summary: Whether the first decimal number is greater than or equal to the second.
details: Vanilla uses it to show something only from a value on, for example when a great holy war's strength progress reaches 50. Write the second number as '(float)50'.

label: At least (whole number)
summary: Whether the first whole number is greater than or equal to the second.
details: Vanilla uses it as the check of a text choice, for example in faith and rite creation texts.

label: At least (unsigned whole number)
summary: Whether the first non-negative whole number is greater than or equal to the second.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: Greater than zero
summary: Whether a whole number is above zero.
details: It is a shortcut for comparing the value with 0.

label: Greater than zero (decimal)
summary: Whether a fixed-point number is above zero.
details: It is a shortcut for comparing the value with 0.

label: Greater than (decimal)
summary: Whether the first fixed-point number is strictly greater than the second.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts, for example for vassal contract obligation levels and oath conditions.

label: Greater than (float)
summary: Whether the first decimal number is strictly greater than the second.
details: Vanilla uses it to show things when a siege's progress passes a value like 50 or 60. Write the second number as '(float)60'.

label: Greater than (whole number)
summary: Whether the first whole number is strictly greater than the second.
details: Vanilla uses it often in texts, for example for legitimacy and merit level checks.

label: Greater than (unsigned whole number)
summary: Whether the first non-negative whole number is strictly greater than the second.
details: The game's texts and GUI files do not use it.

label: GUI editor
summary: Gives access to the game's GUI editor.
details: It is a promote: it turns the global context into the GUI editor object.

label: GUI scope
summary: Gives the top scope of the scripted GUI system, to build a scope from in the interface.
details: Vanilla GUI lines in this list build scopes from it with `SetRoot` and `AddScope` before asking a scripted GUI or script value something.

label: History entry
summary: The history entry the text is about, for example in an artifact's history.
details: It is a promote: it turns the context into a history entry. Vanilla uses it in the artifact history text 'Created by ...'.

label: Holding
summary: A holding, as a game object; the game documents nothing more.
details: It is a promote: it turns the context into a holding. The one text that contains the word, a warning about a holding under construction, writes it as a text variable (`$HOLDING|V$`), so it may not be this function.

label: Holding type
summary: The kind of holding (the central settlement of a barony or county capital) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it for the holding being built and for which holdings a government can hold. In the text about a holding changing, it is the old type and TARGET_HOLDING_TYPE the new one.

label: Holy order
summary: The holy order a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it as the holy order a title is leased out to.

label: Holy site
summary: The holy site a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the holy site that becomes the owner of an artifact, for example when the artifact is enshrined there.

label: Holy site type
summary: The holy site type the text is about.
details: It is a promote: it turns the context into a holy site type. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Hook
summary: The hook (a relationship where one character can get another to do their will) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's messages use it to name the kind of hook gained, or the one an old hook was replaced with.

label: House aspiration
summary: The house aspiration the text is about.
details: It is a promote: it turns the context into a house aspiration. The game's texts do not use it.

label: House relation
summary: The relation between two houses that a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it for the relation's name and the description of its current level, for example in its tooltip and in the message that relations were set up.

label: House relation level
summary: The house relation level a game text is about, such as the level a relation moves to.
details: Vanilla's house relation effect texts name it as the new or starting level of the relation.

label: House relation type
summary: The house relation type the text is about.
details: It is a promote: it turns the context into a house relation type. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Has access to ministry
summary: Whether a character has access to the ministry, judged by a scripted GUI check.
details: It runs the scripted GUI 'tgp_has_access_to_ministry_trigger_gui' with the character as its owner. Vanilla uses it to show or hide parts of the council window. The game's own description ('failed the Children examination') does not match the name or the macro.

label: Has interaction category
summary: Whether a character interaction category exists or applies; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name, it checks for a character interaction category. It returns yes or no. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Checksum differs from compiled
summary: Whether the game's checksum differs from the one it was compiled with.
details: Going by its name only; it returns yes or no. The game's texts do not use it.

label: Has DLC feature
summary: Whether the DLC feature with the given name is available in the game.
details: Vanilla uses it to pick between two texts, for example a building description that changes if the 'tours_and_tournaments' feature is present.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the DLC feature.

label: Has errors
summary: Whether the GUI part it is used on has errors.
details: Going by its name; vanilla uses it as a visibility condition in the shared GUI components file.
